mainTopic: Why the משנה counts eight carrying cases, why two partners in one מלאכה are exempt, and whether moving a loaded body counts as עקירה
overview: The גמרא continues רב מתנא's challenge: the משנה lists eight cases of carrying (יציאות השבת), but there seem to be twelve. Skipping cases that are פטור ומותר explains part of the gap, but the פטור אבל אסור cases still seem to need counting. Along the way, the גמרא asks whether 'exempt and permitted' even exists on שבת, given שמואל's rule. It answers that שמואל meant only cases where a real action is done. The final answer on the count is that the משנה only lists exempt acts that could lead to a חטאת, so lifting counts and putting down alone does not. Next, the גמרא asks how two partners who split one מלאכה can both be exempt, and רבי learns from the word "בעשותה" that only one who does the whole act alone is liable. Finally, רבי rules for רב that a person loaded with food who walks out is חייב, because his body rests in one place, unlike a hand.

steps.title: A partial defense, but the latter section is still difficult
steps.stepSummary: The cases in the first section are not counted because they are פטור ומותר. But the cases in the latter section are פטור אבל אסור, so they should be counted, and the problem remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first set of cases, which are 'exempt and permitted,' the משנה does not bother to teach. But the latter set, which is 'exempt but forbidden,' is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to explain why the משנה lists only eight cases and not twelve. The explanation works for one group of cases but fails for another, so the challenge still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some cases are completely permitted (פטור ומותר), so it makes sense that the משנה skips them. Other cases are forbidden by the רבנן (פטור אבל אסור). Since those are real prohibitions, the משנה should have counted them, so the total should still be twelve.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt and permitted: no punishment and no prohibition at all
exempt but forbidden: no Torah punishment, but prohibited by the רבנן
it is difficult (the problem stands for now; step 5 answers it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of 'exempt.' פטור ומותר means fully allowed. פטור אבל אסור means you may not do it, but there is no Torah punishment.

phrases.english: The first section,
which is exempt and permitted, it does not teach (count).
But the latter section,
phrases.notes: Here אֶלָּא means 'but as for,' not 'rather.'

phrases.english: which is exempt but forbidden, is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בָּבָא דְסֵיפָא, דְּפָטוּר אֲבָל אָסוּר — קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב מתנא's challenge earlier that the משנה should count twelve cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's count of eight carrying cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Skipping פטור ומותר cases explains part of the gap. But פטור אבל אסור cases are real prohibitions and should have been counted, so the number should be twelve.

steps.title: Side question: does 'exempt and permitted' even exist on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: In a side point, the גמרא challenges the idea of פטור ומותר using שמואל's rule. שמואל says every exempt act on שבת is forbidden, except for three specific cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really anything in all of שבת that is 'exempt and permitted'? Didn't שמואל say that every exempt case on שבת is exempt but forbidden, except these three that are exempt and permitted: trapping a deer, trapping a snake, and draining an abscess?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside from the counting problem. It questions the term פטור ומותר that was just used, since שמואל seems to limit it to only three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 assumed the first-section cases are fully permitted. שמואל's rule suggests that almost nothing on שבת is fully permitted. If so, those cases should also be forbidden, and calling them פטור ומותר seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: trapping a deer (sitting in a doorway so a deer already inside cannot leave)

phrases.english: Is there in all of Shabbat 'exempt and permitted'?!
But didn't Shmuel say:
All the exempt cases of Shabbat
are exempt but forbidden,
except for these three, which are exempt and permitted:
trapping a deer, and trapping a snake,
and one who drains an abscess!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא בְּכוּלֵּי שַׁבָּת פָּטוּר וּמוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the term פטור ומותר that step 1 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first-section cases are פטור ומותר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says only three cases on all of שבת are permitted. Any other exempt case, including those in the משנה, should be forbidden.

steps.title: שמואל only meant cases where a real action is done
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's list of three covers only exempt cases where the person actually does an action. There are many exempt cases with no action, and those are fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל needed to list cases, it was for exempt cases where the person does an action. Exempt cases where he does no action are plentiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the side question. It limits שמואל's rule so that the first-section cases can still be פטור ומותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was speaking only about cases where a person performs an act and is still allowed. In the first section of the משנה, the person does nothing, since someone else puts the object into or takes it out of his hand. Cases with no action at all are commonly permitted and fall outside שמואל's list.

keyTerms.meaning: when it was necessary for him (to say this)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a basic tool for the laws of שבת: an exempt case with no real action is not the same kind of case as an exempt case with an action.

phrases.english: When it was necessary for Shmuel (to list them),
it was for exempt cases where he performs an action;
exempt cases where he does not perform an action
there are many.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (שמואל speaks only of cases with an action)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule covers every exempt case on שבת, so nearly nothing is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's rule covers only exempt cases with an action. Cases with no action, like the first section of the משנה, can be fully permitted.

steps.title: Back to the count: there are still twelve
steps.stepSummary: Returning to the main question, the גמרא says that even after the side point, the count still seems to be twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, there are twelve!
steps.whatsHappening: The side question is settled, and the גמרא goes back to רב מתנא's main problem. The latter-section cases are still forbidden, so the total should be twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 only confirmed that the first-section cases can be skipped. The latter-section cases are still פטור אבל אסור. Counting them gives twelve, not eight.

keyTerms.meaning: in any case; regardless (returns to the main point)

phrases.english: In any case, there are twelve!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side branch and returns to the unresolved difficulty of step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פטור אבל אסור cases of the latter section still need to be counted, which makes twelve.

steps.title: The משנה counts only exempt acts that could lead to a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה counts only exempt acts that can lead to liability for a חטאת. Exempt acts that could never lead there are not counted. This solves the twelve-versus-eight problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Exempt cases through which one can come to be liable for a sin-offering, it counts. Those through which one cannot come to be liable for a sin-offering, it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer to רב מתנא. The משנה counts only the forbidden cases that could lead to a full Torah violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting an object (עקירה) is the start of a מלאכה. If the person also put it down in the other domain, he would be liable for a חטאת, so the משנה counts it. Only putting down an object (הנחה) that someone else lifted can never become a full violation, so the משנה leaves it out even though it is forbidden. That leaves eight.

keyTerms.meaning: to liability for a sin-offering (a full Torah violation done unknowingly)
lifting an object from its place (the start of carrying)
putting an object down (the end of carrying)

steps.whatToRemember: Two filters explain why the משנה lists eight: (1) fully permitted cases with no action are not counted; (2) forbidden cases are counted only if they could lead to a חטאת, which means lifting counts and putting down alone does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the משנה chose what to list. Its list is not every prohibition, only the cases connected to a possible full Torah liability.

phrases.english: Exempt cases through which one can come
to liability for a sin-offering, it counts;

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אָתֵי בְּהוּ לִידֵי חִיּוּב חַטָּאת —
phrases.english: those through which one cannot come to liability for a sin-offering,
it does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּטוּרֵי דְּאָתֵי בְּהוּ לִידֵי חִיּוּב חַטָּאת קָא חָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A guiding rule for what the משנה counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every forbidden exempt case should be counted, which gives twelve.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only forbidden cases that could lead to a חטאת (lifting) are counted. Putting down alone is not, so the count is eight.

steps.title: How can both partners be exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה can say both people are פטור when a full מלאכה was actually done by the two of them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says both of them are exempt. But wasn't a forbidden act of work done between the two of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the later section of the משנה, where two people each do half of the carrying out. It asks: how can neither one be guilty if the work was fully done?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full act of הוצאה really happened. One person did the lifting (עקירה) and the other did the putting down (הנחה). Common sense says someone should be responsible, so the גמרא wants a source for exempting both.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden act of work on שבת

phrases.english: Both of them are exempt,
phrases.notes: Quoting the later section of the משנה

phrases.english: but wasn't a forbidden labor done between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the counting question (now solved in step 5) and opens a new question on the משנה's rule that two partners are exempt.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that when one does the עקירה and the other does the הנחה, both are פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full מלאכה was done between them, so it seems unreasonable that nobody is liable.

steps.title: The verse requires one person to do the whole act
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from the words "בעשותה" that only one who does the entire act is חייב. Two people who split it are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי said: the פסוק says "from the people of the land, when he does it." This means one who does all of it, not one who does part of it. One person who did it alone is liable. Two people who did it together are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי learns from a פסוק that liability needs one person to do the complete act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "בעשותה" (when he does it) is read as "when he does all of it." Each partner did only part of the act, so neither fits the פסוק. The work was done, but the Torah only makes someone guilty if he did the whole thing himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
When he does it (the key word in the פסוק)
All of it, the whole act

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the partners did nothing wrong. They are פטור from a קרבן חטאת, but the act is still forbidden.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:
"From the people of the land, when he does it" (ויקרא 4:27)
meaning one who does all of it,
and not one who does part of it.
An individual who did it is liable,
two who did it together are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 with a source from a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural derivation: the Torah itself limits liability to one who does the whole act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a complete מלאכה was done between them, someone should be liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability needs one person to do the complete act ("בעשותה"). Two partners who split it are both exempt.

steps.title: Support from the group of Sages
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר גמדא reports that the same teaching came out of the group of חכמים: one who does it alone is חייב, two who do it are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר גמדא said that it came out from the mouths of the group, and they said: "when he does it" means one person who did it is liable, and two who did it are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings extra support for רבי's teaching. A group of חכמים reached the same reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the law. The point is that the reading of "בעשותה" was accepted by a whole group of חכמים, not just by רבי alone, so the rule is firmly established.
steps.whatToRemember: Two people who split one מלאכה are פטור, because of the word "בעשותה": the Torah only makes a person liable when he alone does the whole act.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said:
It came out from the mouths of the group, and they said:
"When he does it" teaches:
an individual who did it is liable,
two who did it are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 7 with a parallel teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's rule that two who do one מלאכה together are פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching reported by רבי חייא בר גמדא in the name of a group of חכמים, based on the same word "בעשותה".

steps.title: A person loaded with food walks out
steps.stepSummary: רב asks רבי: if a friend loaded food and drink onto a person, and he walked out to the street, is moving his own body like lifting the object?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב asked רבי: if his friend loaded him with food and drink, and he carried them outside, what is the law? Is lifting his body like lifting the object from its place, so he is liable? Or perhaps not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב asks whether a person who never lifted the object with his hand, but walked out with it on his body, has done the needed עקירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally הוצאה needs lifting the object (עקירה) and putting it down (הנחה). Here the friend placed the load on him, so he never lifted it. The only thing he "lifted" was his own body when he started walking. Does that count?

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting / moving his body from its place
Lifting the object from its place

phrases.english: Rav asked Rabbi:
If his friend loaded him with food and drink,
and he carried them outside, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: עֲקִירַת גּוּפוֹ כַּעֲקִירַת חֵפֶץ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: Is lifting his body like lifting the object from its place,
so he is liable,
or perhaps not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: what counts as עקירה when the object rests on the person's body.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether moving one's body while loaded counts as עקירה of the object, making him חייב for הוצאה.

steps.title: He is liable, unlike an object in his hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers that he is חייב, and this case is not like the משנה's case of an object placed in his hand, where he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: he is liable, and it is not like his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rules that the loaded person is חייב. He also points out that this is different from the משנה's case of an object put into someone's hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, if someone puts an object into the hand of the person inside and he pulls his hand out, he is פטור because he did no עקירה. רבי says the body is different: moving the body does count as lifting the object.

keyTerms.meaning: To his hand (the case of an object placed in his hand)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the משנה. An object placed in the hand gives פטור, but an object loaded onto the body gives חייב.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is liable,
and it is not similar to his hand.
phrases.notes: This points back to the משנה's case where an object was placed in his hand and he is פטור.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is חייב. Moving his body counts as עקירה of the object, unlike an object placed in his hand.

steps.title: Why the body is different from the hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reason: a body normally rests in one place, so moving it is a real lifting. A hand does not rest in one place, so moving it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? His body is at rest, but his hand is not at rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי treated the body differently from the hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A body stands in one fixed place, so when it starts moving with the load, that counts as lifting the object from its place. A hand is always moving around and never has a fixed resting place, so moving it is not an עקירה. That is why the משנה's hand case is פטור and the loaded-body case is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: At rest, settled in one place

steps.whatToRemember: A person loaded with an object who walks out is חייב, because his body rests in one place and moving it counts as עקירה. A hand never rests in place, so moving an object placed in it is not עקירה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important rule for הוצאה: what counts as an object's "place" depends on whether what it rests on is normally fixed in place.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
His body is at rest,
his hand is not at rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי's distinction in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The body rests in a fixed place, so moving it counts as עקירה. The hand does not rest in place, so moving it does not.
